author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read FortiManager's own event log, sent over syslog to the data collector. Administrator logins, logouts and login failures go to Auth, configuration events and administrator actions go to ManagementEvent, and other events stay generic. The parsers are children of the built-in Fortinet_Master_non-cef and Fortinet_Event parsers.
notes:
Setup:
- FortiManager's own event log is sent to the data collector over syslog (config system locallog syslogd setting, severity information, csv off). The README has the steps.
- Lines must carry the FortiManager serial (FMG...) in device_id.

Saving in the console:
- The built-in Fortinet_Master_non-cef claims every line and normalizes nothing, and its child Fortinet_Event claims the subtype=system lines and sets only sensor_type FORTIGATE_FW.
- The configuration parser is a child of Fortinet_Master_non-cef, and the Auth and system parsers are children of Fortinet_Event.
- To add each in Sophos Fusion, choose Add Custom Parser, tick Set Global Parent in Parser Script and keep Parent parser (default): the parent picker lists only your own parsers, never built-in ones.
- Paste the whole file, !PARENT line included; its !SCHEMA line sets the schema, whatever the dialog shows.
- Without that option the save fails with "code contains restricted syntax: !PARENT"; turn the option on in the editor and save again.

Field mapping:
- Administrator logins, logouts and login failures (system messages 10018, 10019 and 10014) go to Auth with the user, the address and interface from userfrom, and the session.
- Configuration events (subtypes devcfg, glbcfg, scrmgr, scply, dm, fmwmgr, objcfg and dvm) and the system messages that record an administrator's action, such as CLI commands, setting changes, reboots and policy package locks, go to ManagementEvent with the user, address, interface, operation, change, managed device and ADOM.
- Other events, such as fgfm tunnel status, HA and FortiGuard updates, stay generic.
- The pairs are read with CEF(): in Run Test on 2026-10-16, Sophos NG-SIEM's SPLIT_NAME_VALUES cut a quoted change set that holds " key=" text, and with CEF() all 117 fields matched the emulator.

Time:
- Times come from date, time and tz.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up from the field tables and example in Fortinet's FortiManager Log Message Reference 7.6.

Testing:
- As a sibling of Fortinet_Event, the Auth parser took 3 of 10 lines in a lab tenant on 2026-10-16 with FortiGate events between them, and none after Fortinet_Event took a line; as its child it took 10 of 10.
- Each parser passed Run Test under its built-in parent in a lab tenant on 2026-10-16: 106 of 106 fields matched the emulator, each took its lines in each of 5 runs, also with FortiGate events between them, and none took another parser's line.

Known gaps:
- The csv layout and the log forwarding layout of FortiAnalyzer features aren't covered.
